diagnosis: HBV calibrated with DDS (NSE objective) on the whole period 1971-10 to 1997-12, with a one-year warm-up. Initial stores were set close to their long-term levels (soil 250 mm, lower zone 8 mm). Calibration NSE is 0.854, KGE 0.77 and r 0.93. Simulated flow is about 14% higher in volume than observed (PBIAS +14%), and this bias appears in every calibration. Possible causes are errors in the rainfall or PET forcing, or groundwater leaving the catchment through the chalk/limestone aquifers. The model cannot represent such losses. Recessions and low flows on the permeable part of the catchment are only roughly captured by the single linear lower store (K2≈0.08, PERC≈1.25). Peak timing is reasonable (MAXBAS≈3.5) and the clay soils produce fast quickflow (UZL≈4, K0≈0.68). A split-sample check calibrated on 1971-1984 alone. It gave almost the same parameters (FC≈290, LP≈0.95, BETA≈4.4, K2≈0.077) and NSE 0.84. The model was never run on the 1985-1997 data with these parameters, so this check shows the parameters are stable but does not show how well they predict a new period. Snow parameters have almost no effect (about 1% of precipitation falls as snow) and are poorly identified. I am moderately confident in the parameters and expect an NSE of roughly 0.80-0.85 in 1998-2008. Very wet or very dry years and summer low flows are the most likely weak spots.
